title: the uniform-tile-spacing loop guards itself with num_tile_columns, which is assigned only after the loop, so the guard can never fire
object: H266RawPPS, one allocation holding col_width_val and row_height_val adjacently (libavcodec/cbs_h266.h:594-595)
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: the in-loop check tests num_tile_columns, which holds a stale value throughout because it is assigned from i only after the loop; the real counter i is tested nowhere, so the writes run past col_width_val into row_height_val
allocator_layer: the object IS one allocation and the crossing is interior to it. There is no inner allocator and nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. VVC_MAX_TILE_COLUMNS and VVC_MAX_TILE_ROWS are enum constants in libavcodec/vvc.h and are REDUCED to 20 each: the defect is that the bound check is keyed to a stale counter, so the array's real length changes only how many iterations it takes to leave. The stale guard is reproduced in the buggy arm rather than deleted, so the arms differ by its key.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source: n9.0.1:libavcodec/cbs_h266_syntax_template.c contains the FIXED form `i == VVC_MAX_TILE_COLUMNS` (1 occurrence) and the pre-fix `num_tile_columns > VVC_MAX_TILE_COLUMNS` 0 times. Two-sided. A fix-reversal.
distinguishing: this is the GATE-THAT-CANNOT-FIRE shape in upstream code -- a guard that is present, reads correct, and is keyed to a variable the loop does not update. The two arms therefore differ by the guard's KEY, not by the presence of a guard, which is what makes the reading about the defect rather than about adding a check. No other case in this corpus has that shape.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **NOT CAUGHT; the defect reproduced**: the sequence completed with the crossing made, which the case's own CHECKs place inside ONE allocation, so an allocation-granular bound is in bounds for it. WHAT THIS IMAGE CANNOT SEPARATE: av_malloc and av_refstruct_allocz here are the buffer-pool port's arena carve (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c), which returns an interior pointer carrying the whole metadata arena's bounds, so no per-allocation bound exists in this image at all. The completion is fixed twice over -- the case's CHECKs keep the crossing inside one struct, and the allocator would not have bounded the struct anyway -- and this run cannot tell which. It establishes that the case runs to its defect in a Capstone domain on both arms with no fault anywhere; the 'no allocation-granular bound can see it' claim rests on the CHECKs. Build note: the driver's two aligned_alloc(64, ...) arenas are compiled as malloc, because the application SDK has no aligned_alloc (musl's fallback drags a second malloc into the link); pool-allocator.c aligns every payload from its address, so nothing relies on the arena's alignment. CAPACITY: the driver takes 80 MiB of arenas (FF2_PAYLOAD_BYTES 64 MiB + FF2_META_BYTES 16 MiB), more than the plain corpora's SDKs hold, and the first run on those refused every case at the driver's own allocation check (CONTROL-FAILED 604, recorded, not scored). These rows come from an SDK pair that differs from that one ONLY in heap capacity: level0 arena 128 MiB; Sublet pool 2^27 in a 256 MiB grant.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc8f0e5b8 address=0xc8f51768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image bac4d0e72798ef6b. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED: the sequence completes. The crossing is interior to one allocation, which the case asserts on the offsets, so a per-allocation bound is in bounds for it. NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner; cases 0-2 got their reading from probe cases 40-42 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests, and the same seam is where these will be measured. ARENA CAVEAT, stated rather than left implicit: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (shared/driver.c calls ff2_memory_init on an aligned_alloc) and src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 carves it by bumping a cursor, returning a raw interior pointer and rounding every request up to 64 bytes. __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. So on this harness there is NO per-allocation bound on the struct at all, and a completion here is weaker evidence than 'the bound is the whole allocation' would be. The sub-object claim does not depend on that -- the crossing is interior by construction, which the case asserts on the offsets -- but the arm must not be read as a measured per-allocation bound.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES on both arms and each prints its own VERDICT, so the completion is a reading and not a silent pass. NOT CAUGHT. 22 of 22 arms passed, runner exit 0, with the platform controls firing in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY. THE REASON IS WEAKER THAN 'CHERI BOUNDS THE ALLOCATION AND THE CROSSING STAYS INSIDE', and that is stated rather than glossed: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 bumps a cursor and returns a raw interior pointer, rounding every request to 64 bytes), so there is no per-allocation bound on the struct at all on this harness. The completion shows that nothing bounded anything at this granularity, not that a bound was in force and held. The sub-object claim does not rest on the arm -- the case asserts its own offsets. This is the over-claim that was corrected on the wmem arms, written down before it could be made again. BUILD: clang -O0, purecap, linked against the port's libffmpeg-pool.a from `cmake --preset cheribsd`. -O0 IS LOAD-BEARING: a first suite built -O1 returned VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE for case 0 while the other nineteen arms passed and both controls fired, because case 0's index is a compile-time constant one past its member and clang folded the store away. Rebuilt at -O0 with nothing else changed, it reads DEFECT-REPRODUCED. Reporting the -O1 suite would have recorded a compiler artifact as a CheriBSD reading. Evidence: results/20261006-cheribsd/.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED two-sided 2026-10-06, results/20261006-native-subobject-7/: NO ASan report, and the arm also prints the value it crossed into, so the silence is not the access failing to happen. The positive control fires in the same probe: asan-probe-7.c's 'past' arm, one uint32 past the whole allocation, reports heap-buffer-overflow and exits 1. Built -O0, which is load-bearing -- at -O1 the dead stores are optimised away and the control cannot fire. The probe allocates with plain malloc rather than the port's arena, deliberately: inside a case binary av_malloc carves one arena, so ASan could not see an allocation bound even in principle and a silence there would prove nothing. DETECTOR NOTE: the first run of this probe read as a detection on ALL arms because it grepped for the string 'AddressSanitizer' while the probe leaked, and LeakSanitizer's summary line contains that string. Keyed on heap-buffer-overflow and with the leak fixed, the reading inverts. Recorded because a positive finding from a mis-keyed check is the mirror of a clean zero.
